messages:
omar: Hey folks — since we enabled automatic API key rotation our Go service (go-sdk v1.4.2) has been seeing a lot of requests that just hang ~10-30s and then 504. Not all clients, only ones doing long streaming calls. Tried bumping retries but it just piles up. Any known issues?

jessica: Sorry to hear that, can you paste a minimal snippet of how you attach the token and how rotation runs? Also any client transport config (http.Client / Transport) would help.

omar: Here is the gist of the code we use to attach token and rotate:

```go
// tokenFetcher periodically refreshes token in a global var
var currentToken atomic.Value // string

func attachToken(req *http.Request) {
    req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+currentToken.Load().(string))
}

transport := &http.Transport{
    MaxIdleConns: 100,
    IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{
    Transport: transport,
    Timeout: 0, // we rely on caller contexts
}

// request path
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", apiURL, body)
attachToken(req)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```

We rotate currentToken in a goroutine while requests are in-flight. When rotation happens the long requests stop returning until the client eventually times out / 504 from our reverse proxy.

jessica: Hmm — a few hypotheses: (1) token rotation updates header for subsequent requests but existing TCP connections may reuse an idle connection with the old token (server might respond 401 and your retry handler may be doing curious things). (2) context cancellation vs client timeouts: if callers rely on context cancellation but the SDK library doesn't propagate cancel correctly across retries you can hit a stuck request.

mike: Jumping in — we had a similar report months ago where token refresh + connection reuse interacted poorly with the SDK retry loop. Two practical checks: make sure you set req = req.WithContext(ctx) for each retry attempt (or use req.Clone(ctx)) and ensure your RoundTripper injects Authorization on the actual request that is sent, not only on a prototype req. Also verify Transport.IdleConnTimeout is shorter than your token TTL so stale connections are dropped sooner.

Here are quick repro steps I used locally:

1) small server that validates Authorization header and returns 200 for current token, 401 for others.
2) client does a long streaming POST (50s) using the code above.
3) rotate the token on server side after 5s.

If you run that you will see client-side goroutine stuck until IdleConnTimeout or the outer cancel. Logs: 

```
2026-02-18T14:01:05Z client: POST /v1/stream -> reused connection, sent old auth header
2026-02-18T14:01:06Z server: token invalid, replied 401 (connection kept alive)
2026-02-18T14:01:06Z client: retry loop attempted to resend body but body reader is drained -> blocking
```

Suggested fixes:
- Make token injection per-attempt: use a Transport wrapper that sets Authorization on RoundTrip(req) rather than mutating a shared req ahead of time.
- Use req = req.Clone(ctx) for each retry attempt so the body and context are fresh.
- Set Transport.DisableKeepAlives = false (default) but tune IdleConnTimeout (e.g., 30s) and MaxIdleConnsPerHost to avoid reusing a connection with stale auth for long-lived flows.
- Ensure your retry logic cancels the previous attempt's context before starting a new one to avoid goroutine leaks.

omar: That matches what we saw about body reader drained. Our retry wrapper just loops and calls client.Do(req) without cloning the body. I can change that. Any recommended settings for IdleConnTimeout / MaxIdleConnsPerHost?

mike: For frequent rotation shorter IdleConnTimeout helps (15-30s). For high concurrency increase MaxIdleConnsPerHost (e.g., 100) and set DisableKeepAlives=false so connections are still reused when valid. Also consider using a token refresh hook that pauses issuing new requests during the short rotation window if you can tolerate it.

jessica: Can you try two quick, minimal changes and report back?
1) Change retry to clone request and attach Authorization per-attempt. Example:
```go
for i := 0; i < maxRetries; i++ {
    attempt := req.Clone(ctx)
    attachToken(attempt)
    resp, err := client.Do(attempt)
    if err == nil && resp.StatusCode < 500 { return resp, nil }
    // cancel/close body before next attempt
}
```
2) Lower IdleConnTimeout to 20s and set Transport.MaxIdleConnsPerHost = 200

omar: Will try now and escalate if not fixed. Thanks.

deploy-bot: :rocket: Deployment succeeded for branch token-rotation-fix at commit abc123 (mike)

mike: One more note — we just released go-sdk v1.4.5 which includes a guard that clones requests for retries and a fix to cancel previous attempts on token refresh. If you want to avoid churn, try that version.

omar: Installing v1.4.5 now and will run a soak test. If problems persist I'll drop logs here (including tcpdump) — thanks for the quick triage :pray:

jessica: Great, marking as monitoring. If it still misbehaves tag me and we'll open a support ticket with repro artifacts. :white_check_mark:
